title: DBRE Platform Overview
description: Availability, latency, capacity, and recovery signals for one Postgres environment.

panels.title: Connection saturation

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity) AS current_connections,
                current_setting('max_connections')::int AS max_connections,
                round(
                    100.0 * (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity)
                    / current_setting('max_connections')::int, 1
                ) AS pct_used;

panels.description: Current connections as a percentage of max_connections -- feeds the availability SLI.

panels.title: Connections by state

targets.rawSql:
SELECT state, count(*) AS connections
            FROM pg_stat_activity
            WHERE pid <> pg_backend_pid()
            GROUP BY state
            ORDER BY connections DESC;

panels.description: Current connection count grouped by state (active, idle, idle in transaction, ...).

panels.title: CPU utilization

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity) AS current_connections,
                current_setting('max_connections')::int AS max_connections,
                round(
                    100.0 * (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity)
                    / current_setting('max_connections')::int, 1
                ) AS pct_used;

panels.description: Current connections as a percentage of max_connections -- feeds the availability SLI.

panels.title: Long-running queries

targets.rawSql:
SELECT pid, usename, state, now() - query_start AS duration, left(query, 200) AS query
            FROM pg_stat_activity
            WHERE state != 'idle'
              AND now() - query_start > interval '30 seconds'
              AND pid <> pg_backend_pid()
            ORDER BY duration DESC;

panels.description: Queries running longer than 30 seconds, oldest first.

panels.title: Blocking locks

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                blocked.pid AS blocked_pid,
                blocked.usename AS blocked_user,
                blocking.pid AS blocking_pid,
                blocking.usename AS blocking_user,
                blocked.query AS blocked_query
            FROM pg_stat_activity AS blocked
            JOIN pg_locks bl ON bl.pid = blocked.pid AND NOT bl.granted
            JOIN pg_locks kl ON kl.locktype = bl.locktype
                AND kl.database IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.database
                AND kl.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.relation
                AND kl.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.page
                AND kl.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.tuple
                AND kl.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM bl.transactionid
                AND kl.pid != bl.pid AND kl.granted
            JOIN pg_stat_activity AS blocking ON blocking.pid = kl.pid;

panels.description: Sessions that are blocked, and who is blocking them -- the first query to run during a 'everything is slow' incident.

panels.title: Top queries by total time

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                left(query, 200) AS query,
                calls,
                round(total_exec_time::numeric, 1) AS total_ms,
                round(mean_exec_time::numeric, 2) AS mean_ms,
                round((100 * total_exec_time / sum(total_exec_time) OVER ())::numeric, 1) AS pct_of_total
            FROM pg_stat_statements
            ORDER BY total_exec_time DESC
            LIMIT 20;

panels.description: The queries consuming the most cumulative execution time -- start here for tuning work.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                sum(heap_blks_hit) AS heap_hit,
                sum(heap_blks_read) AS heap_read,
                round(
                    sum(heap_blks_hit) / nullif(sum(heap_blks_hit) + sum(heap_blks_read), 0)::numeric, 4
                ) AS cache_hit_ratio
            FROM pg_statio_user_tables;

panels.description: Buffer cache hit ratio -- sustained values below ~0.99 usually mean shared_buffers is too small for the working set.

panels.title: Read/write latency

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                sum(heap_blks_hit) AS heap_hit,
                sum(heap_blks_read) AS heap_read,
                round(
                    sum(heap_blks_hit) / nullif(sum(heap_blks_hit) + sum(heap_blks_read), 0)::numeric, 4
                ) AS cache_hit_ratio
            FROM pg_statio_user_tables;

panels.description: Buffer cache hit ratio -- sustained values below ~0.99 usually mean shared_buffers is too small for the working set.

panels.title: Database size

targets.rawSql:
SELECT datname, pg_size_pretty(pg_database_size(datname)) AS size
            FROM pg_database
            WHERE datistemplate = false
            ORDER BY pg_database_size(datname) DESC;

panels.description: On-disk size of every database in the cluster.

panels.title: Largest tables / bloat estimate

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                relname AS table_name,
                pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(relid)) AS total_size,
                n_live_tup,
                n_dead_tup,
                round(100.0 * n_dead_tup / nullif(n_live_tup + n_dead_tup, 0), 1) AS pct_dead
            FROM pg_stat_user_tables
            ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(relid) DESC
            LIMIT 20;

panels.description: Largest tables and a coarse dead-tuple ratio as a bloat proxy.

panels.title: Index usage

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                schemaname, relname AS table_name, indexrelname AS index_name,
                idx_scan, pg_size_pretty(pg_relation_size(indexrelid)) AS index_size
            FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
            ORDER BY idx_scan ASC, pg_relation_size(indexrelid) DESC
            LIMIT 20;

panels.description: Indexes that are rarely or never scanned -- candidates for removal.

panels.title: Autovacuum health

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                relname AS table_name,
                last_autovacuum,
                last_autoanalyze,
                n_dead_tup,
                n_mod_since_analyze
            FROM pg_stat_user_tables
            ORDER BY n_dead_tup DESC
            LIMIT 20;

panels.description: Tables overdue for autovacuum relative to their dead-tuple ratio -- a leading indicator of both bloat and transaction-ID wraparound risk.

panels.title: Replication lag

targets.rawSql:
SELECT
                application_name,
                client_addr,
                pg_wal_lsn_diff(pg_current_wal_lsn(), replay_lsn) AS lag_bytes,
                extract(epoch FROM (now() - reply_time)) AS lag_seconds
            FROM pg_stat_replication;

panels.description: Replica lag in bytes and seconds, run on the primary. Empty result means no replicas attached (expected for a standalone local demo instance).
